papers.head: PRUITT'S · GAS · GIFTS · BAIT — HOME OF BIGFOOT

pages.text:
Marcy,

I've taken the kids to the shelter. If you find this, come straight there.

Do *NOT* go to the military checkpoint, they don't know what they're dealing with.

That witch has been burying things in the woods for weeks.

Rifle's in the safe, but she's empty, never found the right rounds. Combination's on my keys.

E.

Saw it again today, up the north ridge. Taller than any man, and it just watched me, calm as you like, then walked off into the trees without a sound. Sheriff laughed me out of the office. Marcy believes me though. That's enough.

Opened the store. Everyone thinks it's a gag, the signs, the casts, the photos. Let them. Keeps the lights on, and it keeps me out here, where I can watch.

Put trail cams up along the old logging trails this spring. If he's out there, I'll get him on film, and then they'll all stop laughing.

Seven years of watching, and I've stopped wanting to prove anything to anybody.

He came down to the creek at dusk again, near enough I could hear him breathing. Just sat there across the water with me a while, then went on his way.

Whatever he is, he's no danger to anyone. I've gotten fond of the big fella. I think he's been out here alone a long time.

Thirteen years of trail cams, and I've caught the big fella maybe twice, both times a blur. Suits us both fine. But this year I'm getting something else. Something fast.

Camera four, three nights running now, a shape going through the trees quicker than anything should move. Low to the ground, wrong somehow.

It isn't him. He's gentle. This thing isn't.

The lights started a few weeks back, out past the government land. Then the animals went quiet.

Camera four's got that fast shape every night now, closer to the road each time.

Checked the shelter today, restocked it, oiled the hatch. Dug that hole myself years ago, half as a joke. Hope to God I never need it.

papers.head: FIELD REPORT · CHECKPOINT 7 · ROUTE 9 TRANSFER POINT

pages.text:
FROM: OIC, CP-7
TO: CONTAINMENT CMD (BY RELAY)
SUBJ: LOSS OF CONTAINMENT, CONVOY 3

1. At 0140 the specimen in C-7 broke its restraints in transit. The container failed from the *inside*. Two men lost at the trailer.

2. Specimen not recovered. Last seen moving south, low over the treeline. Do not engage it in the open.

3. Brood cargo (C-9 and crates 1-6) intact. Recommend sealed transfer. No firing near the crates.

4. Since 0200 our casualties are getting back up. Treat all personnel KIA as hostile. Head shots are no good while they've got their helmets on.

5. I have ordered the line held at the barricade. Relay down. Nothing from command since 0150.

6. To whoever reads this: the line is gone. Whatever was south of the cordon is north of it now.

CPT R. MERCER, OIC


(in pencil, under it)
They're at the sandbags. Going up the tower with what's left.

C-3   BIO SAMPLES (CHILLED)      12 CS
C-4   SPECIMEN, INTACT, RESIN     1 U
C-7   ██████████████████     1 U
C-9   BROOD, LIVE                  6 CRT

ORIGIN:  SITE 4 (MINE WORKINGS)
DEST:    ██████████

HANDLING:
- NO LIGHT IN C-7.
- NO NOISE NEAR C-9.
- C-4 DOES NOT LEAVE THE RESIN.

RECEIVED CP-7: ___________

Scrambled to intercept. Contact low over the ridge, south of CP-7. No transponder. Lights: green, purple, moving like nothing with wings.

Ordered to force it down. (draft)

0124. It fired first. A beam, not tracer. Port engine gone.

Hit it twice with the guns. It's trailing something, losing height, limping south.

We're going in. If anyone finds this: it came down south of the cordon, and it's not one of ours. (draft)

BENEATH THIS STONE
THE PEOPLE OF HEMLOCK GAP
HAVE LAID A RECORD FOR THEIR CHILDREN'S CHILDREN.

TO BE OPENED OCTOBER 13, 2003.

SHOULD THE VOICE IN THE TREES EVER CALL AGAIN,
DO NOT WAIT. OPEN THIS.
WE HAVE SET DOWN WHAT WE LEARNED.

*ANSWER IT NOT.*

JOSIAH TULLY · ELI TULLY, HIS SON
LEVI PRUITT
HATTIE BELL McCOY · AGED 9
SHE WENT TO HER FATHER'S VOICE
MARY SIZEMORE TATE
WILLIAM GENTRY · RUTH GENTRY
THOMAS ASHBY · MARTHA ASHBY
CORA DEAN · AGED 6
JOHN HENRY WAYCASTER

ALL OCTOBER 13, 1903
TAKEN INTO THE TREES. NO BODY LIES HERE.

Scratched into the back of the last stone, by another hand: AMOS PRUITT. WENT AFTER LEVI. OCT. 15.

Eleven stones, cut alike. The turf in front of them has never been dug.

papers.head: Hemlock Gap · set down this 20th day of November, 1903

pages.text:
To whoever opens this.

We are the people of Hemlock Gap, what is left of us. Our pastor writes this for all of us, for he has the best hand, and because he was there.

In the spring of this year the railroad came to cut its line through the forest from east to west. The company paid well and we were glad of it. Forty of our men worked the felling. They cut a strip of open ground a hundred feet wide clean across the wood, and the rails were laid in it.

We did not know what we were cutting.

The first was Josiah Tully's girl, Ada Mae, in August. She went to the edge of the cut at dusk because she heard her mother calling her in. Her mother was at the stove. Ada Mae walked into the trees and was not seen again.

After that it came most nights. It called from the woods in voices we knew. A man's wife. A child's father. The dead, sometimes. It called our names. *It knew our names.*

Those who answered it, or went to it, did not come back. We found no blood and no bodies. Only their lanterns, set down neat in the leaves, still burning.

On the night of October the 13th it called from every side of the town at once, and eleven of ours went out to it. Hattie Bell McCoy was nine years old. She went to her father's voice. Her father was standing beside me.

We searched until morning, and the morning after. Old Mrs Sizemore, who was raised on the ridge, told us where they had gone. There is a place behind this one, she said: the same woods made over wrong, and the voice keeps what it takes there. She said the way in is a staircase that stands in the woods by itself.

Amos Pruitt found the staircase, a half day east of here, in a clearing where nothing grows. Clean steps, painted, a carpet up the middle, like the stairs in a fine house. No house. He drew it for me and I have put his drawing here.

He went up it after his brother Levi. He came down before dawn, alone, white to the hair. He said every clearing up there has four ways out. His brother's voice called down two of them, and he could not bear to take the way that was silent. He said the silent way was the true one. He knew it, and he could not do it.

He went back up the next night and did not come down.

What stopped it was older than this church. The ridge folk always said the wood had a keeper, a tall shape seen at the edge of things, that keeps the forest whole. We called him *the Keeper*. The railroad's cut had parted his country in two, and where the land was severed, the voice came through.

In October we carried what Mrs Sizemore told us to carry across the cut, and buried it there, and bound the two halves of the wood together again in the Keeper's name. *Where the Keeper is, the voice is not.* It went quiet that night, and it has stayed quiet.

We never got our people back.

We have put this record in the ground by the church where it will keep, and set a date on it a hundred years off, so that no one will dig it up out of curiosity while any of us are living.

But if it calls again, do not answer it. Do not follow it. Mend the land, and find the Keeper.

And if you go up those stairs after someone you love, *take the silent way.* Take it every time, whatever you hear.

God keep you. We could not.

Rev. Elias Marsh, for Hemlock Gap
